item: A core-dump verdict carries the stack systemd-coredump logged for the previous process (cut from the front to 739 serialised bytes)
summary: journalctl -o short-iso prints a core-dump entry's thread headers and frames as indented continuation lines that name no pid, so the pid filter dropped them. They are now read from the entry whose header names the pid, scrubbed as one block BEFORE any cut, and kept in journal order (#0 upward) until the next whole line would pass COREDUMP_STACK_BYTES (739); frames_dropped and bytes_dropped count the rest. Tested on the documented format only; not yet run against a real journal.
